summary: US officials are searching for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange in an attempt to pressure him not to publish thousands of confidential diplomatic cables.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange surfaces in Brussels after nearly a month in hiding, saying he does not fear for his safety but is on permanent alert and has been advised by his lawyers not to travel to the US.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is scheduled to speak at the Centre for Investigative Journalism summer school at City University London.

Wikileaks founder Julian Assange said the organisation is working through a backlog of further secret material and expects a substantial increase in whistleblower submissions after publishing more than 92,000 classified US military logs on the Afghanistan war.

Swedish prosecutors revoked an arrest warrant for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange after an on-call prosecutor had issued it over a rape allegation, and a higher-ranked prosecutor found no grounds to suspect him of rape.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange denies allegations of rape and sexual molestation after a Swedish arrest warrant was issued and then withdrawn.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange accused Wired magazine of having an agenda, not checking facts, and spreading misinformation about WikiLeaks, including a claim that the site was preparing to release hundreds of thousands of classified US documents from the Iraq war.
Julian Assange helped orchestrate the biggest leak in the history of the world, publishing a flood of classified documents that went to the heart of America's military and foreign policy operations.
Julian Assange and his lawyer threatened to sue The Guardian over its planned publication of US embassy cables, leading to a negotiated delay.

A Swedish court approves a request by prosecutors to detain Julian Assange for questioning on suspicion of rape, sexual molestation and unlawful coercion, and prosecutors say they will seek his arrest through Interpol.

Interpol added WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange to its worldwide wanted list on sex-crime allegations from Sweden, as the US announced an active criminal investigation into whether he violated espionage laws.
WikiLeaks, led by Julian Assange, released hundreds of classified US embassy cables, after which Assange was forced into hiding and faced an extradition case over an alleged rape in Sweden.
Julian Assange's lawyer disputed the validity of a Swedish arrest warrant for rape allegations, saying it was improperly certified and that Assange denies the accusations.
Swedish authorities issue a new arrest warrant for Julian Assange over sexual crime allegations, which he denies.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is scheduled to answer Guardian readers' questions in a live online Q&A, subject to his access to an internet connection.

Swedish prosecutors issued a fresh request to British police to extradite WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange over sex offence allegations, after mistakes in the original European arrest warrant had prevented any move to apprehend him.
Julian Assange agreed to meet British police to discuss sexual assault allegations in Sweden, though he was not arrested and his legal team planned to fight extradition.
Julian Assange was denied bail by a London judge over Swedish sexual assault allegations and was remanded in Wandsworth prison until 14 December.
Julian Assange was arrested by UK police, initiating a fast-tracked extradition process under a European Arrest Warrant to return him to Sweden for questioning regarding a rape charge.
Julian Assange is expected to appear in a UK court after his lawyers said he would meet British police to discuss a European arrest warrant from Sweden relating to alleged sexual assaults.

Julian Assange faces mounting pressure as Swedish prosecutors pursue rape, sexual molestation, and unlawful coercion allegations against him, while WikiLeaks faces financial and infrastructure attacks.

A disaffected former colleague of Julian Assange, Daniel Domscheit-Berg, prepares to publish a tell-all book about WikiLeaks, as Assange faces denied bail over sexual assault allegations and financial and server setbacks.

US politicians and pundits from both parties intensify calls for action against WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, with Republicans labeling him a terrorist and leading Democrats calling for his prosecution.
Lawyers for Julian Assange said they are preparing for a possible US indictment, though no charges have yet been lodged.
Julian Assange, speaking from his Wandsworth prison cell, urges supporters to protect WikiLeaks from "instruments of US foreign policy."
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is scheduled to appear in a London court to seek release from prison on bail after being remanded in custody over Swedish sexual assault allegations.
Julian Assange remains in custody despite being granted bail by Westminster magistrates court, after the Swedish government appealed the decision.
UK authorities, not Swedish prosecutors, made the decision to keep Julian Assange in a London jail and oppose his bail, as confirmed by the Swedish prosecutor's office.
The high court will hold a hearing on a Swedish appeal against bail for Julian Assange, the founder of WikiLeaks.
Julian Assange was granted bail.

A US congressional committee hears testimony from lawyers about the possibility of prosecuting Julian Assange under the Espionage Act, with lawyers expressing consensus that an indictment is likely though extradition from Britain is doubtful.

Julian Assange's barrister Geoffrey Robertson QC described Sweden's three categories of rape in court during Assange's bail hearing, as Assange had not been formally charged and his lawyers disputed whether the European Arrest Warrant was for questioning or prosecution.
Julian Assange said his life and the lives of his WikiLeaks colleagues are under threat, speaking outside Ellingham Hall after his release on bail.
A Belarusian state newspaper said WikiLeaks had allowed the dictatorship to identify organizers, instigators and rioters, including foreign ones, who had protested against rigged elections.
Julian Assange is reported to have sold his memoirs to publishers Canongate in the UK and Knopf in the US, though Canongate refused to confirm or deny the story.
Julian Assange says his fate would rest in David Cameron's hands if the US charges him with espionage, and that it would be politically impossible for Britain to extradite him.
Julian Assange said he expects to earn more than £1m from book deals, including an autobiography, to fund legal costs and keep WikiLeaks afloat while fighting extradition to Sweden.
A Guardian book reveals that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange disguised himself as an old woman in a wig for fear he was being followed by US intelligence.
A book titled "Wikileaks: Inside Julian Assange's War on Secrecy" by Guardian journalists David Leigh and Luke Harding is published.
Julian Assange's legal team argues that human rights considerations and the threat of further extradition from Sweden to the US should prevent his extradition under a European arrest warrant.

Former WikiLeaks spokesman Daniel Domscheit-Berg claims Julian Assange threatened to sue him over his memoir portraying Assange as power-obsessed, and alleges he took the submission system when he left the organization.

Julian Assange's lawyer made a graphic defence during an extradition hearing at Belmarsh magistrate's court, arguing that the sexual assault allegations against the WikiLeaks founder would not amount to rape under English law.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange applied to trademark his name for use in public speaking, journalism, and entertainment services.

A Matrix Chambers barrister predicted it is "very likely" that a senior district judge will order Julian Assange's extradition to Sweden to face sexual assault charges, dismissing his defence team's preliminary arguments.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange loses his extradition battle at Belmarsh Magistrates' Court and is to be extradited to Sweden to face allegations of rape and sexual assault, though his legal team confirms he will appeal.
Lawyers for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange lodged papers to appeal against his extradition from Britain to Sweden to face allegations of rape and sexual assault.
Julian Assange's million-pound memoir deal has collapsed after he became unhappy with the process and no longer wished to write the initially envisaged book.

Julian Assange appeared at the High Court in London at the start of his latest fight against extradition to Sweden over sex allegations, with his new legal team arguing that the European arrest warrant is invalid.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange revealed his intention to make public all 250,000 raw US State Department cables, regardless of possible reprisals to named individuals.
Australia's attorney general confirmed WikiLeaks' unredacted cable release identified at least one Australian intelligence officer, and Julian Assange could face prosecution in Australia as a result.

Julian Assange's publishers, Canongate, released his "unauthorised autobiography" despite his attempt to withdraw from the book deal, prompting Assange to accuse the publisher of "profiteering from an unfinished and erroneous draft."
The high court dismissed Julian Assange's appeal against extradition to Sweden to face rape and sexual molestation claims.
Julian Assange seeks to apply for a supreme court hearing to appeal against extradition to Sweden to face sex crime allegations.

Two high court judges certified a question of general public importance, permitting Julian Assange to petition the supreme court directly within 14 days to ask it to hear his appeal against extradition to Sweden.
A panel of seven UK supreme court justices is to hear Julian Assange's appeal against extradition to Sweden, with a two-day hearing scheduled to begin on 1 February.
Julian Assange enters the final stage of his legal battle to avoid extradition to Sweden, with his legal team appealing to the UK Supreme Court.

The UK Supreme Court heard arguments on the second day of Julian Assange's appeal against extradition to Sweden, with Sweden's legal representative defending the European arrest warrant as validly issued by a public prosecutor.
Julian Assange loses extradition appeal.
Lawyers for Julian Assange formally ask the UK supreme court to reopen his appeal against extradition to Sweden over alleged sex crimes.
The UK Supreme Court reaffirmed its rejection of Julian Assange's appeal against extradition to Sweden and dismissed a last-minute application to reopen the case.
Julian Assange requests political asylum at Ecuador's embassy in London to avoid extradition to Sweden.
Julian Assange takes refuge in the Ecuadorian embassy in London, where he remains outside the reach of UK authorities but can be arrested if he leaves.
Julian Assange is in the Ecuadorian embassy and has asked for political asylum.
A group of public figures, including Michael Moore, Oliver Stone, Daniel Ellsberg, and Noam Chomsky, signed an open letter urging Ecuador to grant Julian Assange political asylum.
Julian Assange refuses to surrender to London police and remains in the Ecuadorean embassy while seeking political asylum.
Ecuadorian officials say President Rafael Correa has agreed to grant Julian Assange asylum, though Correa denies a decision has been made.

Ecuador's foreign minister says Britain has told Ecuador it believes officials can enter its London embassy and arrest Julian Assange, who has been inside the embassy for two months seeking to avoid extradition to Sweden.
Ecuador grants political asylum to Julian Assange, prompting a diplomatic row with the UK and Sweden.

Ecuador's president Rafael Correa is expected to announce whether the country will grant Julian Assange asylum, as Ecuador's foreign minister rejects a British letter warning that the UK could arrest Assange at its embassy in London.

Ecuador remains willing to negotiate with Britain over Julian Assange's fate and proposes that the UK and Sweden undertake not to extradite him to a third country, specifically the US, after the Swedish investigation.
Julian Assange, speaking from the Ecuadorian embassy in London, urged the US to release Bradley Manning and end its "witch-hunt" against WikiLeaks.
A police officer accidentally revealed a restricted document indicating plans to arrest Julian Assange "under all circumstances" if he leaves the Ecuadorean embassy in London.
Benedict Cumberbatch is reported to be in line to play Julian Assange in a forthcoming DreamWorks biopic based on books about WikiLeaks.
Julian Assange's book "Cypherpunks: Freedom and the Future of the Internet" is published.
Julian Assange revealed his intention to run for a Senate seat in the 2013 Australian federal election.

Julian Assange described the forthcoming Hollywood film The Fifth Estate as a "massive propaganda attack" on WikiLeaks and an inflammatory attack on Iran during a video-linked talk to students at Oxford University.
Principal photography began on The Fifth Estate, a film about WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, with Benedict Cumberbatch starring as Assange.

WikiLeaks, with Julian Assange stating it had worked for the past year to analyze the data, publishes more than 1.7m US diplomatic and intelligence records from 1973 to 1976 in a searchable collection called the Public Library of US Diplomacy.
Oliver Stone reveals he met Julian Assange at the Ecuadorian embassy in London and criticises two forthcoming films about the WikiLeaks founder.
US prosecutors alleged during the Bradley Manning trial that Julian Assange built close ties with Manning, guided his document leaks, and advised him on avoiding detection.
Ecuador's foreign minister Ricardo Patino is to visit London to meet Julian Assange at the Ecuadorian embassy, on the eve of the first anniversary of Assange living there.

Ecuador's president Rafael Correa told Julian Assange to stop using the Ecuadorean embassy in London to make fun of Australian politicians during his Senate election campaign, saying he can campaign politically but not mock Australian politicians or people.

Julian Assange's lawyer calls on the US Department of Justice to make a formal statement that it will not prosecute Assange, following off-the-record reports that the department is unlikely to press charges.

Julian Assange is writing a major new book, When Google Met WikiLeaks, to be published in September, recounting his 2011 meeting with Google chairman Eric Schmidt and detailing his vision for the future of the internet.

A Swedish court schedules a hearing for 16 July in the Julian Assange rape case, the first formal legal discussion since 2012, after prosecutors reject his lawyers' request to hand over new evidence and withdraw his arrest warrant.
Stockholm city court decides to keep the detention order against WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange.
Ecuador reaffirms the political asylum granted to Julian Assange two years ago and reiterates its request for safe passage so he can travel to Ecuadorian territory.
Julian Assange says he is leaving the Ecuadorian embassy.

Ecuador's foreign minister accuses the British government of violating Julian Assange's human rights and having no real interest in finding a diplomatic solution to his confinement in Ecuador's London embassy.
Stockholm's appeal court rejects Julian Assange's lawyers' demand to lift the arrest warrant against him.
Julian Assange's lawyers ask Sweden's supreme court to lift the arrest warrant against him, arguing that his confinement in the Ecuadorian embassy is unreasonable and disproportionate.
The French government rejected Julian Assange's asylum request, stating he was not in immediate danger.

Swedish prosecutors dropped investigations into some sexual assault allegations against Julian Assange after the statute of limitations expired, but said they would continue to pursue an interview over an outstanding rape allegation.
Scotland Yard called off its 24-hour surveillance of the Ecuadorian embassy where Julian Assange has been living, though it said the operation to arrest him continues.
The Metropolitan police confirmed that Julian Assange would be arrested if he left the Ecuadorian embassy in London to go to hospital for a medical examination.
Lawyers for Julian Assange say they are considering launching a fresh appeal against his Swedish arrest warrant following the publication of correspondence between British and Swedish prosecutors.

A United Nations panel concluded that Julian Assange's three-and-a-half years in the Ecuadorian embassy amount to arbitrary detention, though the finding is not legally binding and Sweden and the UK disputed it.
Julian Assange says he will leave the Ecuadorian embassy in London if a United Nations panel rules against his claim that he is being illegally detained.
Julian Assange accused UK Foreign Secretary Philip Hammond of insulting the United Nations after Hammond rejected a UN panel finding that Assange’s circumstances amount to arbitrary detention.
The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention is expected to formally publish an opinion that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is being arbitrarily detained, a finding the article disputes.
A UN panel found Julian Assange to be arbitrarily detained and called for his release, but Britain and Sweden rejected the findings and he remained in Ecuador's London embassy.

A UN working group opinion concludes that Julian Assange has been arbitrarily detained in the Ecuadorian embassy, a finding disputed by one member who argues Assange is a fugitive evading arrest rather than being detained.
A UN working group declares WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange to be arbitrarily detained, a finding rejected by British newspapers.
A UN working group issued an arbitrary detention decision concerning Julian Assange, prompting debate over freedom and the rule of law.
David Cameron says Julian Assange should leave the Ecuadorian embassy and submit to a Swedish arrest warrant over rape allegations, dismissing a UN panel finding of arbitrary detention as ridiculous.
The British government formally asks a United Nations panel to review its finding that Julian Assange is arbitrarily detained in the Ecuadorian embassy in London.
WikiLeaks representative Jacob Appelbaum said at a Cannes Q&A that Julian Assange would find life no easier under a President Hillary Clinton, citing Clinton's displeasure over the Cablegate leak.
Julian Assange said WikiLeaks is preparing to publish more emails Hillary Clinton sent and received while US secretary of state.
Sweden's court of appeal will debate whether to grant Julian Assange an open court hearing in his renewed campaign to rescind the arrest warrant against him.
The questioning of Julian Assange by Swedish prosecutors at the Ecuadorean embassy in London was postponed until mid-November.
WikiLeaks says Ecuador intentionally cut off Julian Assange's internet access at the Ecuadorian embassy in London.

Ecuador temporarily restricted Julian Assange's internet access at its London embassy, citing WikiLeaks publications impacting the US election campaign, while the US and Ecuador denied conspiring to silence him.
Julian Assange was questioned at the Ecuadorean embassy in London by an Ecuadorean state attorney and a Swedish prosecutor over 2010 rape allegations.
Julian Assange released a statement detailing his answers to Swedish investigators regarding rape allegations, prompting his accuser's lawyer to accuse him of violating her client in the media.
Julian Assange participated in a Reddit Ask Me Anything session, facing questions about his links to Russia and addressing rumors that he was no longer alive.
Ecuadorian presidential candidate Guillermo Lasso said he would give Julian Assange 30 days' notice to leave the Ecuadorian embassy if he wins the presidency.
US Attorney General Jeff Sessions says arresting WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is a priority, and CNN reports authorities have prepared charges against him.

Swedish prosecutors close their rape investigation into Julian Assange, while the US Department of Justice has not yet filed charges or an extradition request, though Attorney General Jeff Sessions says prosecuting WikiLeaks is a priority.
Julian Assange cancelled a planned press conference at the Ecuadorian embassy in London where he was to make a "special announcement," reportedly to allow negotiations with UK authorities to proceed.
A recut of Laura Poitras's documentary portrait of Julian Assange, updated to reflect WikiLeaks's involvement in leaking Democratic National Committee emails, is reviewed.
Julian Assange promised over a million WikiLeaks releases in 2013.
Julian Assange's lawyer says the WikiLeaks founder is in 'fighting spirit'.
Julian Assange bail hearing
Julian Assange's supporters and lawyer react to extradition verdict.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange launches attack on US politicians in a video.
Julian Assange is fighting extradition to Sweden, a case described as the tip of the iceberg amid broader concerns about Europe's fast-track extradition system.
